name: BaByliss trimmers/stylers
lead: BaByliss is a French personal-care brand, owned by the American group Conair since 1995, that sells hair dryers, straighteners, curling irons, clippers and beard trimmers.[1] People use its clippers and trimmers at home, and barbers use the BaBylissPRO line, to hold a clean hairline, a sharp fade and a crisp beard line, the edges that make a haircut and a jaw look deliberate and defined.[1][2]

A clipper cuts with two comb-like blades, one sliding sideways against the other, powered by a magnetic, rotary or pivot motor.[2] Guards and blade settings control how much hair is left, so one tool can produce a buzz cut, a tapered side or a line-up around the forehead, ears and neck.[2]

The brand began when hairdressers René Lelièvre and Roger Lemoine invented an electric hair straightener in Montmartre; Jean-Pierre Feldblum marketed it as BaByliss in July 1960.[1] Its professional line has since made a point of motors developed with Ferrari engineers, such as the Volare X1 clipper, which the retailer Beautylish describes as using a high-torque DC motor and Japanese-made blades.[3] No published studies have tested these devices.

chain: Clipper or trimmer blades cut hair to a set length
Hairline, fade and beard lines are made crisp
A sharper, cleaner-edged haircut and beard
angle.text: Clippers and trimmers let people set hair length and cut precise lines around the hairline, sideburns, neckline and beard. The result is a defined outline that makes the cut and facial hair look intentional, and regular touch-ups at home keep it that way between barber visits.

infobox: France, marketed as BaByliss from July 1960[1]

paras: BaByliss sells hot tools (dryers, straighteners, curlers) alongside grooming tools. BaBylissPRO is the professional line aimed at salons and barbershops, and BaByliss for Men, launched in 2003, covers beard and body trimmers and clippers.[1]

Within the professional range, the FX family of clippers and trimmers is marketed around Ferrari-designed motors, and the Volare X1 is described as pairing a high-torque DC motor developed with Ferrari engineers with blades manufactured in Japan and a 45-degree cutting edge that keeps hair in the guide longer.[3] Since 2010, BaBylissPRO has also produced hair dryers with engines designed with input from Ferrari engineers.[1]

Clippers use two comb-like blades, one sliding sideways against the other, to cut hair with a scissor-like action, and motors are of magnetic, rotary or pivot types.[2] Low blade friction, kept up by lubrication, is described as important, and ceramic blades resist corrosion and stay sharp longer but are brittle and costly to replace.[2] Blades are usually rust-resistant stainless steel.[2]
Blade numbers set the length left: fine zero blades leave the least hair, a number 1 blade leaves about 1.6 mm, regrowing in about 3.5 days, and a number 2 leaves about 6.4 mm.[2]

The company expanded across Western Europe, and Conair bought a majority share in February 1995; at that point about 45 percent of sales were abroad, mainly through subsidiaries in Germany, England, Belgium, the Netherlands and Spain.[1] Appliances are made at several Conair plants, including one in Chiuduno, Italy acquired from Coif'In in 2009, and reported 2024 revenue was about 175 million euros.[1]
Wikipedia notes that BaByliss is among the brands affected by counterfeit products.[1]

Manual clippers were invented around 1855 by Serbian barber Nikola Bizumić.[2] Leo J. Wahl patented what is described as the first electric hair clipper by 1921, and Mathew Andis entered the market in the same year; John Oster joined in 1928.[2]

card.summary: A French-origin, Conair-owned brand of clippers, trimmers and hot tools used to keep fades, hairlines and beard lines crisp.

quick.overview:
BaByliss makes hair dryers, straighteners, curling irons, clippers and beard trimmers. The brand began in France in 1960 and has been owned by Conair since 1995.

For looks, clippers and trimmers set hair length and cut precise lines around the hairline, neckline and beard, so fades and beard edges stay sharp. The professional BaBylissPRO line is aimed at barbers and salons.
quick.how: Clippers cut with two close-fitting blades, one moving sideways against the other, driven by a motor. Guards and blade numbers set the length left, and trimmers are used for outlines and edges. Blades are kept lubricated and cleaned between uses.
quick.risks: Risks are those of any grooming tool: nicks and skin irritation from close cutting. Blades need lubrication, ceramic blades can break, and counterfeit versions of the brand are common.
